rounds.text: Sejal Glass Ltd demonstrates exceptional financial momentum, underscored by a compounded sales growth of 109% over 5 years [E14] and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 93% [E19]. This top-line and bottom-line expansion is reinforced by elite profitability metrics, including a 31.1% return on equity [E13] and an operating margin expanding to 17% in September 2026 [E26], easily outpacing sector median profit growth of 22.4% [E68]. Valuation and intrinsic assessments further validate the opportunity, as a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 1358 per share against the current market price of Rs 845 [E40], offering a substantial 37.8% margin of safety [E41]. Technical strength matches fundamental quality, with the price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E45, E46]. Conceded: debt exceeds net worth with a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x [E32], and promoters have reduced their stake to 69.08% [E36].

Sejal Glass Ltd carries structural financial risks and a demanding valuation that the underlying stability does not fully support. The company trades at a P/E of 25.87x and an EV/EBITDA of 14.14x, both of which sit at a premium to sector benchmarks of 21.86x and 12.44x respectively [E6, E11]. Furthermore, the price-to-book ratio is elevated at 6.21x against a sector benchmark of 2.42x [E7]. Beneath these stretched valuation multiples lies concerning leverage, as debt to equity stands at 1.21x with total borrowings expanding to Rs 210 Cr in September 2026, creating a clear leverage risk where debt exceeds net worth [E32, E34]. This heavy borrowing burden is compounded by a stark free cash flow deficit of Rs -46 Cr in March 2026 despite reported profits [E31]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing growth metrics and high returns on equity [E13, E16, E19]. However, insider behavior adds to the uncertainty, with promoter holdings declining by nearly 10 percentage points from 78.96% in December 2023 to 69.08% in September 2026 alongside negative institutional money flow [E36, E39]. Finally, historical volatility is exceptionally high at 7809.9%, accompanied by a poor Sharpe ratio of 0.25 and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -100.0%, signaling severe underlying price instability [E48, E49, E50].

The bear highlights a premium P/E of 25.87x and EV/EBITDA of 14.14x against sector benchmarks [E6, E11], but completely ignores that this superior pricing power is fully justified by top-tier fundamentals, including an exceptional ROE of 31.1% [E13] and a rules-based screen scoring a high-confidence 95 out of 100 [E60]. While the bear points to a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x [E32], it glosses over the massive +188.9% surge in Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) to Rs 26 Cr [E35], proving that borrowings are being actively deployed into high-return expansion rather than idle consumption. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -46 Cr in March 2026 [E31], yet operating cash flow simultaneously reached a robust Rs 51 Cr with a healthy cash conversion ratio of 1.76x, demonstrating that profits are fully backed by actual cash generation [E29, E30]. Regarding the bear's concern over promoter holding declines [E36], domestic institutions have aggressively stepped in, increasing their stake by +4.39 percentage points [E38] to back the company's phenomenal 5-year sales growth of 109% [E14]. Finally, the bear's reliance on historical volatility metrics [E49] is rendered irrelevant by current price action, where the stock is trading comfortably above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 [E45, E46].

Conceded: the company delivered a robust operating cash flow of Rs 51 Cr in March 2026 with a cash conversion ratio of 1.76x [E29, E30]. However, the bull's dismissal of the negative free cash flow of Rs -46 Cr ignores the very real cash drain driven by heavy investments [E31]. While the bull points to a +188.9% surge in CWIP to Rs 26 Cr to justify leverage [E35], borrowings actually expanded to Rs 210 Cr in Sep 2026 alongside a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x, meaning debt exceeds net worth and creates tangible leverage risk [E32, E34]. Furthermore, the bull celebrates domestic institutional buying [E38] while ignoring the broader reality of net negative institutional money flow and a promoter stake reduction down to 69.08% [E36, E39, E65]. The bull's reliance on moving averages and a relative-strength rating of 100 [E45, E46] masks the alarming historical record of a -100.0% peak-to-trough drawdown and extreme annualised volatility [E48, E49]. Finally, despite reporting profits, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E57].

While the bear highlights negative free cash flow [E31], this is the direct result of a massive 188.9% surge in capital work-in-progress [E35] aimed at fueling trailing twelve-month sales growth of 52% [E16] and profit growth of 93% [E19]. Conceded: debt-to-equity stands at 1.21x with borrowings of Rs 210 Cr [E32, E34], yet this leverage is efficiently deployed to generate a superior 31.1% return on equity [E13] and 18.6% ROCE [E12], both of which significantly exceed sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. The bear's concern over promoter stake reduction [E36] and institutional outflow [E39, E65] ignores that domestic institutions have simultaneously built a 4.39% position from zero [E38], while the stock maintains a perfect relative-strength rating of 100 [E46]. Historical volatility and drawdowns [E48, E49] are outweighed by a current rules-based screen score of 95 out of 100 [E60] and the fact that profit growth has exceeded price growth by 99%, indicating the business is starting to outperform market expectations [E52]. Finally, conceded: the company pays no dividends [E4, E57], but the 37.8% margin of safety relative to intrinsic value [E41] and a 1.76x cash conversion ratio [E29] suggest that capital is being effectively retained to maximize shareholder value through growth.

While the bull attributes negative free cash flow of Rs -46 Cr [E31] to growth-oriented capital work-in-progress [E35], this spending is sustained by rising borrowings that have reached Rs 210 Cr [E34]. Conceded: the company reports high ROE and ROCE [E13, E12], yet this performance is built on a debt-to-equity ratio of 1.21x [E32], creating a leverage risk that the market has already priced at a significant premium to sector benchmarks for P/E, P/B, and EV/EBITDA [E6, E7, E11]. The bull's emphasis on domestic institutional entry [E38] fails to account for the massive 9.88 percentage point reduction in promoter holdings [E36] and the overall negative institutional money flow [E39, E65]. Furthermore, a high rules-based score [E60] does not erase the extreme risk signaled by a historical -100% drawdown [E48] and annualized volatility of 7809.9% [E49]. Finally, the lack of dividends [E4, E57] and inconsistent operating-margin trends [E27, E28] undermine the bull's valuation case, particularly as the stock has delivered a -6% price return over the last year [E22] despite the claim that profit growth is outperforming expectations [E52].
